features.accounts: The app creates or uses an account, including one created automatically (guest or device account).
features.purchases: Any in-app purchase, consumable, non-consumable or subscription, through any billing system.
features.ads: Any advertising SDK or ad placement, including rewarded ads.
features.game_economy: A virtual currency or item economy: buying, earning, staking, losing or transferring in-app value, including service credits that can be wagered or won.
features.kids: Children are a target audience, or the app is in a kids or Families program. Decide false from the console target audience or age rating plus the absence of a kids category or Families enrolment (an Apple export may not show the category; a rating above the kids bands with no child-directed content is enough); decide true from any of those or child-directed content.
features.ugc: Users can publish content other users see: text, names, images, chat, profiles. Decide false when the code has no path that publishes one user's content to another (no posting, chat, public profile or shared name); a permission string alone does not make it true.
features.ai: Generative AI output or user data sent to a model provider.
features.health: Health, fitness, medical or wellness data or claims, HealthKit or Health Connect.
features.sensitive_permissions: Permissions or APIs a store restricts or asks to declare: Google restricted permissions, background location, foreground services, full-screen intent, accessibility, VPN; on iOS, Always location, background modes and tracking. A purpose string or manifest entry counts even when no code uses it, because the store sees the declaration. Ordinary runtime permissions (camera with a purpose string) do not.
features.regulated: Activity that needs a licence or regulated entity in some territory: finance, crypto, gambling with real value, medical, insurance, legal services.
features.third_party_login: Sign-in through a third-party or social login service (Apple counts this for 4.8).
